newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PNG army demands sacking of government - radio.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PNG army demands sacking of government - radio.

text.p: Papua New Guinea's defence force commander and police commissioner have demanded the sacking of the government over its use of mercenaries on Bougainville, Australian Broadcasting Corporation radio reported on Monday.

The ABC said the Papua New Guinea Defence Force Commander Jerry Singirok and the police commissioner had visited the country's governor-general and asked him to sack the government of Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan.
The ABC reporter said Singirok had earlier told troops in the capital Port Moresby that he did not agree with the use of mercenaries and had asked them not to make trouble.
Papua New Guinea has hired 40 mercenaries to train troops in a bid to end a nine-year rebellion on Bougainville island by the Bougainville Revolutionary Army.
Australia's Labor opposition called on Canberra on Friday to cut aid to Australia's small northern neighbour after it stood firm on sending mercenaries into Bougainville.
Thousands of people have been killed in the secessionist rebellion.
